ai.definition: RAG Pipelines (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) combine the strengths of retrieval-based systems with generative models to produce coherent and contextually accurate outputs.
ai.howItWorks: RAG pipelines first retrieve relevant information from a database or knowledge base, then use this retrieved data as input for a generative model to generate a response. This two-step process ensures that the generated content is both relevant and contextually accurate.
ai.problemSolved: Addressing the limitations of purely generative models in producing coherent and contextually accurate responses by integrating retrieval capabilities.
ai.buildProcess: Develop and train a retrieval model to efficiently search for relevant information, then integrate this with a generative model that can produce coherent text based on the retrieved data. Fine-tuning both models together is crucial for optimal performance.
ai.costDrivers: Data storage costs, computational resources required for training and inference, and ongoing maintenance of the retrieval and generation models.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: growing adoption in advanced AI applications and content generation
ai.regulation: Regulatory frameworks are still developing; however, data privacy and intellectual property rights will be key considerations.
ai.risks: Dependence on the quality of the underlying database, potential biases in retrieved information, and challenges in ensuring coherent and contextually accurate outputs.
ai.profitability: High potential for profitability due to its application in advanced AI applications and content generation but requires significant investment in development and maintenance.
ai.futureDevelopment: Continued improvement in both retrieval efficiency and generative model accuracy, as well as integration with other AI technologies like machine translation and summarization.

glossary.def: A technology that combines retrieval of relevant information with generative models to produce coherent and contextually accurate outputs.
Machine learning models designed to generate new data instances similar to a training dataset, often used for tasks like text generation or image synthesis.
